hooks.text: There are more planets than stars in the night sky.
Alien worlds actually outnumber the stars in our galaxy.
Over 100 billion planets orbit inside the Milky Way.

title: There Are More Planets Than Stars
description: Our home galaxy is crowded with more than just suns. New data reveals that planets actually outnumber stars in the night sky.

beats.text: There are more planets than stars in the night sky.
beats.visual: Milky Way night sky view from Earth, 2020

beats.text: We once thought our galaxy was a collection of lonely suns.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of stars floating in the void

beats.text: Edwin Hubble proved we're one galaxy among billions in the 1920s.
beats.visual: Photograph of Edwin Hubble at the 100-inch Hooker Telescope

beats.text: This barred spiral home holds up to 400 billion stars.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the Milky Way barred spiral structure
queries: Milky Way galaxy artist concept illustration
Milky Way spiral structure top view

beats.text: It hides a black hole four million times heavier than the Sun.
beats.visual: Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A star
queries: Sagittarius A black hole Event Horizon Telescope photo

beats.text: But scientists realize the stars aren't the main event.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a lonely exoplanet in space

beats.text: The Milky Way actually contains at least 100 billion planets.
beats.visual: Cluster of various artistic exoplanets in a dark void

beats.text: That's an average of one world for every single star.
beats.visual: Illustration of an exoplanet orbiting a bright sun

beats.text: It means there are more planets than stars in the night sky.
beats.visual: Wide panoramic view of the Milky Way over a desert landscape
queries: Milky Way band night sky panorama
